record.title: The cohomological modularity conjecture for Q_3
record.statement: Let $Q_3$ be the quotient variety associated with the involution $\iota_3$. A **strongly rigid resolution** is a resolution of singularities with the rigidity property intended in the paper, and let the newform of weight $6$ and level $8$ determine its associated Galois representation. **Cohomological modularity conjecture for $Q_3$.** The variety $Q_3$ admits a strongly rigid resolution of singularities for which the representation on $H^5$ coincides with that obtained from the newform of weight $6$ and level $8$ up to semisimplification. The preceding discussion shows that $Q_3$ has a resolution of Kodaira dimension $0$ under the stated hypotheses; the stronger modularity and rigidity assertion remains conjectural.

record.title: Conjecture on maximal sum-free sets in type I groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of type I, and let $\mu(G)$ be the size of a largest sum-free subset of $G$, while $f_{\max}(G)$ is the number of maximal sum-free subsets of $G$. **Type I maximal-sum-free-set conjecture.** Except for the groups $\mathbb{Z}_2^k$, all type I groups $G$ have exponentially fewer maximal sum-free sets than $2^{\mu(G)/2}$.

The conjecture identifies $\mathbb{Z}_2^k$ as the likely extremal exception among type I groups. The paper proves the assertion for broad classes, but notes that new ideas are needed for the remaining even-order groups with many elements of order $2$; the full claim remains open.

record.title: Bollobás–Gyárfás conjecture on highly connected monochromatic subgraphs
record.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, and let a **2-coloring** assign one of two colors to every edge. A subgraph is **$k$-connected** if its vertex connectivity is at least $k$.

**Bollobás–Gyárfás conjecture.** If $n>4(k-1)$, then every 2-coloring of $K_n$ contains a monochromatic $k$-connected subgraph of order at least

$$
n-2(k-1).
$$

The conjecture concerns the largest highly connected monochromatic subgraph forced in every 2-coloring of a complete graph; the supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.

record.title: Ellis et al.'s extremal conjecture for intersecting families of permutations
record.statement:
Let $d4d5$ be the set of permutations in $d4d5_{n,n,n}$, and call $d4d5$ $t$-intersecting when any two members agree on at least $t$ points. For each admissible $i$, let $d4a2_i$ be the family defined by requiring at least $t+i$ fixed points among the first $t+2i$ points. **Ellis et al.'s conjecture.** If $d4d5 \subseteq \mathscr{P}_{n,n,n}$ is a $t$-intersecting family, then

$$
|\mathscr{F}| \leq \max_i |\mathscr{G}_i|.
$$

Furthermore, equality holds only if $d4d5$ is isomorphic to $d4a2_i$ for some $i$. This conjecture extends Erdős–Ko–Rado-type extremal results to permutations and predicts that the largest intersecting families are among the canonical families $d4a2_i$; its resolution is not supplied here.

record.title: Stanley's conjecture on decompositions of k-fold acyclic complexes
record.statement:
Let $\Delta$ be a simplicial complex. For $\sigma\in\Delta$, write $\operatorname{link}_\Delta\sigma$ for its link. The complex $\Delta$ is **$k$-fold acyclic** if $\operatorname{link}_\Delta\sigma$ is acyclic over a field $\Bbbk$ for every $\sigma\in\Delta$ with $|\sigma|<k$. A **rank $k$ boolean interval** is an interval in the face poset isomorphic to the Boolean lattice on $k$ elements.

**Stanley's conjecture.** If $\Delta$ is a $k$-fold acyclic simplicial complex, then its face poset can be decomposed into disjoint rank $k$ boolean intervals whose minimal faces together form a subcomplex of $\Delta$.

The conjecture generalizes Stanley's rank-$1$ decomposition theorem for complexes acyclic over a field. The paper provides an explicit counterexample, so the conjecture is refuted, while also proving a weaker version and a special case.
record.source_name: Joseph Doolittle and Bennet Goeckner, “Resolving Stanley's conjecture on k-fold acyclic complexes”, arXiv:1811.08518 (2021).

record.title: The low BKL-exponent obstruction conjecture for L-space branched covers
record.statement: Let $L$ be a prime, fibred, strongly quasipositive link. Write $k(L)$ for its **BKL-exponent**, defined as the maximum integer $k$ such that $L$ is the closure of $\delta_n^kP$ for some $n\geq 2$, $k\geq 0$, and BKL-positive braid $P\in B_n$. **Low BKL-exponent obstruction conjecture.** If $k(L)\leq 1$, then no cyclic branched cover $\Sigma_n(L)$ is an L-space. Together with the stated characterization of simply laced arborescent links for BKL-exponent at least $2$, this would prove the broader conjectural classification of prime fibred strongly quasipositive links with an L-space cyclic branched cover. The supplied text does not resolve this case.

record.title: Kézdy–Snevily conjecture for the covering function of permutation space
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{S}_n$ be the set of permutations of $[n]=\{1,2,\dots,n\}$, with Hamming distance $d_H$. Define $f(n,s)$ to be the minimum size of a subset of $\mathcal{S}_n$ having covering radius at most $n-s$. **Kézdy–Snevily conjecture.** If $n$ is even, then $f(n,2)=n$; if $n$ is odd, then $f(n,2)>n$. The conjecture is motivated by its implications for the latin-square transversal conjectures, and the paper proves that its odd-$n$ case implies the whole conjecture. The source gives no resolution status for the conjecture itself.

record.title: Uniqueness conjecture for optimal hyperplane covers of extremal matrices
record.statement:
Let $A$ be a multidimensional $(0,1)$-matrix. An **extremal matrix** is one with no polydiagonal that becomes to contain a polydiagonal after changing any zero entry to one. An **optimal hyperplane cover** is a minimum-weight hyperplane cover of $A$.

**Uniqueness conjecture.** Every extremal matrix has the unique optimal hyperplane cover.

The conjecture asserts the proposed one-to-one correspondence between extremal multidimensional matrices and their optimal hyperplane covers. The paper reports no counterexamples and proves the claim for some classes of extremal matrices; its general status is not established here.

record.title: Sandon's translated-points conjecture for contactomorphisms
record.statement:
Let $(V,\xi)$ be a closed contact manifold, where $\xi$ is a cooriented contact structure, and let $\operatorname{Cont}_0(V,\xi)$ denote the identity component of its contactomorphism group. Fix a contact form $\alpha$ with $\xi=\ker\alpha$. A point $x\in V$ is an $\alpha$-translated point of a contactomorphism $\phi$ if

$$
\exists s\in\mathbb{R}\quad\text{such that}\quad \phi(x)=\phi_\alpha^s(x)\quad\text{and}\quad (\phi^*\alpha)_x=\alpha_x,
$$

where $\{\phi_\alpha^t\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$ is the Reeb flow of $\alpha$. **Sandon's translated-points conjecture.** For every $\phi\in\operatorname{Cont}_0(V,\xi)$ and every contact form $\alpha$, the number of $\alpha$-translated points of $\phi$ is at least the number of critical points of a function. The conjecture predicts an analogue of the Arnold conjecture for contactomorphisms, replacing fixed points by translated points. The source does not specify the function or provide evidence resolving the conjecture, so its precise lower bound and status should be checked against the surrounding paper or cited literature.

record.title: Trivial-torsion conjecture for four-longitude sutured monopole Floer homology
record.statement:
Let $G_{\mathrm{tor}}$ be the torsion group appearing in Lemma 4. The group is associated to the monopole Floer homology computation for the closure of $(V,\gamma^4)\sqcup(V,\gamma^4)$.

**Trivial-torsion conjecture.** The torsion group $G_{\mathrm{tor}}$ in Lemma 4 is trivial:

$$
G_{\mathrm{tor}}=0.
$$

The conjecture arises from an expected direct computation of the monopole Floer homology of a particular closure constructed by Kronheimer and Mrowka. The preceding rank calculations constrain the torsion, but do not determine it completely.

record.title: The maximum-width conjecture for hollow three-dimensional convex bodies
record.statement:
A **hollow convex body** is a three-dimensional convex body whose interior contains no lattice point. The **width** of a convex body is the minimum, over nonzero integer linear functionals, of the difference between its maximum and minimum values on the body. Let $w_c(3)$ denote the largest width of a hollow three-dimensional convex body. The tetrahedron constructed in the paper has width $2+\sqrt2$. **Maximum-width conjecture.** The tetrahedron in the construction is the convex $3$-body of largest width; equivalently, 
$$
w_c(3)=2+\sqrt2.
$$
 The construction establishes the lower bound $w_c(3)\geq 2+\sqrt2$; the conjecture asserts that this bound is sharp.

record.title: Littlewood's maximum-order conjecture for the Riemann zeta function on the 1-line
record.statement:
Let $\zeta(s)$ denote the Riemann zeta function, let $T\geq 1$, and write $\gamma$ for the Euler–Mascheroni constant. **Littlewood's maximum-order conjecture.**

$$
\max_{t\in [1,T]}|\zeta(1+it)|\sim e^\gamma\log\log T.
$$

This conjecture predicts the precise maximal order of the zeta function on the line $\operatorname{Re}(s)=1$, refining known lower bounds and conditional upper bounds. A more precise version is attributed in the source to Granville and Soundararajan; the source does not state that the conjecture has been resolved.

record.title: Song–Cai–Yue rate conjecture for sequentially recoverable locally recoverable codes
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ denote an $(n,k,r,t)_{\text{seq}}$ code over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. Let

$$
m=\lceil \log_r(k) \rceil.
$$

**Song–Cai–Yue conjecture.** An achievable upper bound on the rate $k/n$ is

$$
\frac{k}{n} \leq \frac{1}{1+\sum_{i=1}^{m}\frac{a_i}{r^i}}, \qquad a_i\geq 0,\quad a_i\in\mathbb{Z},\quad \sum_{i=1}^{m}a_i=t.
$$

This conjecture concerns the maximum achievable rate of sequentially recoverable locally recoverable codes from any number of multiple erasures. The paper presents it as a conjectured tight rate bound; its resolution is not established in the supplied text.

record.title: Campos et al.'s Hilton condition conjecture for 3-clique graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a 3-clique graph, and let Hilton's condition mean the condition for a simple graph with an even number of vertices and a universal vertex that

$$
|E(\overline{G})|+\alpha(\overline{G})<\frac{|V(G)|}{2},
$$

where $\alpha(\overline{G})$ is the cardinality of a maximum independent set of edges of $\overline{G}$. **Campos et al.'s conjecture.** The graph $G$ is type-II if and only if it satisfies Hilton's condition. The conjecture seeks to extend Hilton's characterization from the stated universal-vertex setting to 3-clique graphs; no resolution is given in the supplied text.

record.title: Minimum distance conjecture for complete intersection ideals
record.statement:
Let $I\subset S:=K[t_1,\ldots,t_s]$ be a complete intersection graded ideal of dimension $1$, generated by forms $f_1,\ldots,f_c$ with $c=s-1$, where $d_i=\deg(f_i)$ and $2\leq d_i\leq d_{i+1}$ for $i\geq 1$. Suppose that the associated primes of $I$ are generated by linear forms. **Minimum distance conjecture.** For integers $d$, $k$, and $\ell$ satisfying

$$
1\leq d\leq \sum_{i=1}^{c}(d_i-1)-1,
$$

$$
0\leq k\leq c-1,\qquad d=\sum_{i=1}^{k}(d_i-1)+\ell,\qquad 1\leq \ell\leq d_{k+1}-1,
$$

one has

$$
\delta_I(d)\geq (d_{k+1}-\ell)d_{k+2}\cdots d_c.
$$

The conjecture holds when an initial ideal of $I$ with respect to some monomial order is a complete intersection, but remains open in general; it is sharp for vanishing ideals in the range where the minimum distance exceeds $1$.
record.source_name: Susan M. Cooper, Alexandra Seceleanu, Stefan O. Tohaneanu, Maria Vaz Pinto and Rafael H. Villarreal, “Generalized minimum distance functions and algebraic invariants of Geramita ideals”, arXiv:1812.06529 (2019).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.06529

record.title: The rainbow antichain-union conjecture
record.statement:
Let $A_k$ be an antichain of size $k$, and let $\bigvee_s$ and $\bigwedge_s$ denote the posets consisting respectively of a common minimal or maximal element together with $s$ incomparable elements. Let $F(n,l,P)$ be the maximum size of a color class in an $l$-coloring of $B_n=2^{[n]}$ with no rainbow copy of $P$. **Rainbow antichain-union conjecture.** For any $k,s$ and $l\ge k+s+1$,

$$
F(n,l,\vee_s+A_k)=F(n,l,\wedge_s+A_k)=o(2^n).
$$

The conjecture extends the preceding bounds for disjoint unions of antichains with fork-shaped posets; no resolution is supplied in the source.

record.title: Homma–Kim's conjectural bound for rational points on even-dimensional hypersurfaces
record.statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power, let $m\geq 4$ be even, and let ${\mathcal X}\subset {\mathbb P}^m$ be a hypersurface of degree $d$ defined over ${\mathbb F}_q$. Define

$$
\theta_q(j)=1+q+\cdots+q^j
$$

for $j\geq 0$, and set $\theta_q(j)=0$ for $j<0$.

**Homma–Kim's conjecture.** The number of rational points satisfies

$$
|{\mathcal X}({\mathbb F}_q)|\leq \theta_q\left(\frac{m}{2}-1\right)\left((d-1)q^{\frac{m}{2}}+1\right).
$$

This conjecture refines the previously known upper bound for nonsingular hypersurfaces in even-dimensional projective spaces, whose bound is never attained. The paper proves the conjecture in the threefold case $m=4$, thereby determining the maximum number of rational points on nonsingular degree-$d$ threefolds in ${\mathbb P}^4$ for the relevant range of parameters.

record.title: Conjectured upper bound for the maximum modulus of graph independence roots
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\textnormal{maxmod}(n)$ denote the maximum modulus of an independence root among graphs on $n$ vertices. **The maximum-modulus conjecture.** For $n\ge 3$, 

$$
\textnormal{maxmod}(n)\le \begin{cases} 2\cdot 3^{\frac{n-3}{3}}+\frac{n}{3} & \text{if } n\equiv 0 \pmod 3,\\ \\ 3^{\frac{n-1}{3}}+\frac{n-1}{3} & \text{if } n\equiv 1 \pmod 3,\\ \\ 4\cdot 3^{\frac{n-5}{3}}+\frac{n+1}{3} & \text{if } n\equiv 2 \pmod 3.\end{cases}
$$

The bound is presented as a computational conjecture based on computations with Maple and nauty; its resolution is not specified in the source.
record.source_name: Jason I. Brown and Ben Cameron, “Maximum Modulus of Independence Roots of Graphs and Trees”, arXiv:1812.09775 (2018).

record.title: Approximation of statistical dimension by distance to the scaled subdifferential
record.statement:
Let $f$ be one of the objectives $f_2$, $f_3$, $f_5$, or $f_6$ described in the preceding remark, let $\overline{x}$ be the signal under consideration, and let $X\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I)$. For $\tau\geq 0$, define

$$
J(\tau):=\mathbb{E}\left[\operatorname{dist}^2(X,\tau\partial f(\overline{x}))\right].
$$

**Approximation conjecture.** For these choices of $f$, the statistical dimension is well approximated by the squared Euclidean distance to the scaled subdifferential:

$$
\min_{\tau\geq 0}J(\tau)\approx\delta(\partial f(\overline{x})).
$$

The claim is motivated by empirical results and is intended to provide an approximation when explicit formulas for $J$ and its minimum are unavailable for the constrained objectives. Its validity is not established in the supplied text.

record.title: Aharoni–Howard rainbow matching conjecture
record.statement:
Let $H_1,\dots,H_k$ be $r$-uniform hypergraphs on the same set of $n$ vertices. Define $f(n,r,k)$ to be the smallest $m$ such that every $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices with $m$ edges has a matching of size $k$.

**Aharoni–Howard's conjecture.** If each $H_i$ has $f(n,r,k)$ hyperedges, then there is a rainbow matching

$$
\{e_1,\dots,e_k\},\qquad e_i\in E(H_i)\text{ for }i=1,\dots,k.
$$

This is a rainbow version of the Erdős–Ko–Rado matching threshold. It is proved for balanced $r$-partite hypergraphs when $r=3$, while the general statement remains open.

record.title: Small-gap limiting law for Gaussian beta ensembles
record.statement:
Let $\beta>0$, and let the Gaussian beta ensemble G$\beta$E have joint density

$$
\frac{1}{Z_{n,\beta}}e^{-n\beta \sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i^2/2}\prod_{1\leq i<j\leq n}|\lambda_i-\lambda_j|^\beta.
$$

Let $t^n_{k,\beta}$ be its $k$-th smallest gap. **Small-gap conjecture.** There exists a constant $c_\beta$ depending on $\beta$ such that

$$
\tau^n_{k,\beta}=c_\beta n^{(\beta+2)/(\beta+1)}t^n_{k,\beta}
$$

has limiting density

$$
\frac{\beta+1}{(k-1)!}x^{k(\beta+1)-1}e^{-x^{\beta+1}}
$$

as $n\to\infty$. This conjecture extends the observed smallest-gap laws for the Gaussian orthogonal and unitary ensembles, and proposes the same limiting behavior as for circular beta ensembles.

record.title: Simplex-code conjecture for functional batch codes
record.statement:
Let $r$ be a positive integer, and let the $[2^r-1,r]$ simplex code be the binary simplex code of length $2^r-1$ and dimension $r$. Let $FB(r,k)$ denote the minimum number of servers in a functional $k$-batch code with $r$ information symbols. **Simplex-code conjecture.** The $[2^r-1,r]$ simplex code is a functional $2^{r-1}$-batch code, and consequently

$$
FB(r,2^{r-1})=2^r-1.
$$

This is presented as a conjecture motivated by constructions of parallel RIO and functional batch codes; the stated equality is verified in the examples discussed for $r=3,4,5$, while the general assertion remains open.

record.title: Classification conjecture for TPMSg3s with order-3 and order-4 screw symmetry
record.statement:
A TPMSg3 is a triply periodic minimal surface of genus $3$. Consider TPMSg3s with an order-4 screw symmetry and TPMSg3s with an order-3 screw symmetry. The named surfaces tP, tD, CLP, tG, H, rPD, and rGL are examples with the respective screw symmetries.

**Screw-symmetry classification conjecture.** The tP, tD, CLP, and tG surfaces are the only TPMSg3s with an order-4 screw symmetry. The H, rPD, and rGL surfaces are the only TPMSg3s with an order-3 screw symmetry.

This is a stronger symmetry-based classification formulation than the preceding family statement. The source raises it after noting that order-2 rotations around horizontal axes were used only to determine the López--Ros factor, and gives no resolution.

record.title: Reading's maximum cd-index conjecture for Bruhat intervals
record.statement: Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system, and let $[u,v]$ be an interval in the Bruhat order of $W$. Write $k$ for the length of $u$ and suppose that the length of $v$ is $n+k+1$. The $cd$-index of a dual stacked $n$-polytope with $n+k+1$ facets is understood coefficientwise. **Reading's conjecture.** The $cd$-index of $[u,v]$ is coefficientwise less than or equal to the $cd$-index of a dual stacked $n$-polytope with $n+k+1$ facets. In particular, the $cd$-index of an interval $[1,v]$ is less than or equal to the $cd$-index of a Boolean lattice. Bruhat intervals are Eulerian and shellable, and Reading showed that their $cd$-indices span the generalized Dehn--Sommerville space. The proposed coefficientwise maximum remains unresolved in the source.
record.source_name: Margaret M. Bayer, “The cd-Index: A Survey”, arXiv:1901.04939 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.04939

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2019).

record.title: Ruzsa's conjecture on spanning size in abelian groups of finite torsion
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an abelian group with finite torsion $r$, and let $A$ be a finite subset of $G$. Write $A+A=\{a+b\mid a,b\in A\}$ and let $\langle A\rangle$ be the smallest subgroup or coset of a subgroup containing $A$. The doubling constant is $|A+A|/|A|$.

**Ruzsa's conjecture.** If there exists a constant $K$ such that

$$
\frac{|A+A|}{|A|}\leq K,
$$

then there exists a constant $C\geq 2$ such that

$$
\frac{|\langle A\rangle|}{|A|}\leq r^{CK}.
$$

This conjecture predicts that the exponential dependence on the doubling parameter in the Freiman--Ruzsa theorem is essentially optimal, while replacing the theorem's much larger exponent by a linear function of $K$. The supplied text gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Yifan Jing and Souktik Roy, “Small doublings in abelian groups of prime power torsion”, arXiv:1901.05606 (2019).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2019). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1212.5738](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.5738).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.05606

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2019).

record.title: Repeated orthonormal sequence threshold conjecture for p-frame energy
record.statement: Let $N=m+kd$ points be given in $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$, where $1\leq m<d$ and $d\geq 2$, and let $\mathbf{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times N}$ be their Gram matrix. The repeated orthonormal sequence is $\{e_{j\bmod d}\}_{j=1}^N$, and its energy is $d(k^2-k)+2k$. **Repeated orthonormal sequence threshold conjecture.** There is a value $p_0$, independent of $d$ and $m$, such that the repeated orthonormal sequence minimizes $E_p$ over all systems of $N$ unit vectors for $p<p_0$, while the minimum satisfies $E_p(\mathbf{A})<d(k^2-k)+2k$ for $p>p_0$. Moreover, $p_0=p_0(k)$ satisfies $p_0(k)\to2$ as $k\to\infty$.
record.source_name: Alexey Glazyrin and Josiah Park, “Repeated minimizers of p-frame energies”, arXiv:1901.06096 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.06096

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2019).

record.title: Győri's conjecture on bipartite Turán numbers of even cycles
record.statement:
For a graph $H$, let $ex(m,n,H)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $H$-free bipartite graph with parts of sizes $m$ and $n$. Let $C_{2t}$ denote the cycle of length $2t$.

**Győri's conjecture.** Suppose that $m,n,t$ are integers satisfying $n\geq m^2$ and $m\geq t\geq 3$. Then

$$
ex(m,n,C_{2t})\leq (t-1)n+m-t+1.
$$

Győri disproved this conjecture for $t=3$, and Balbuena, García-Vázquez, Marcote, and Valenzuela further disproved it when $t\leq \frac{m+1}{2}$. The source says that it remains open when $t\geq \frac{m}{2}+1$.
record.source_name: Binlong Li and Bo Ning, “Exact bipartite Turán numbers of large even cycles”, arXiv:1901.06137 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.06137

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2019). “As far as we know, this conjecture remains open when $t\geq \frac{m}{2}+1$.”

record.title: A sharp bipartite Turán formula for large even cycles
record.statement:
For a graph $H$, let $ex(m,n,H)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $H$-free bipartite graph with parts of sizes $m$ and $n$. Let $C_{2t}$ denote the cycle of length $2t$.

**Sharp bipartite Turán formula.** Suppose that $m,n,t$ are positive integers satisfying

$$
n\geq m\geq t\geq \frac{m}{2}+1.
$$

Then

$$
ex(m,n,C_{2t})=(t-1)n+m-t+1.
$$

This conjecture is presented as a sharpening of the remaining open range of Győri's conjecture, and the supplied parser gives no resolution evidence for it.
record.source_name: Binlong Li and Bo Ning, “Exact bipartite Turán numbers of large even cycles”, arXiv:1901.06137 (2019).

record.title: The minimal degree conjecture for standard identities of matrix Grassmann algebras
record.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative unital ring, let $m,n\geq 1$, and let $E^{m}$ be the $m$-generated Grassmann algebra

$$
E^{m}=R\langle v_i\mid 1\leq i\leq m\rangle/(v_i^2,v_iv_j+v_jv_i\mid 1\leq i,j\leq m).
$$

For $k\geq 1$, the standard polynomial is

$$
s_k(x_1,\ldots,x_k)=\sum_{\pi\in\mathfrak{S}_k}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)x_{\pi(1)}\cdots x_{\pi(k)}.
$$

It is a standard identity of degree $k$ for $M_nE^m$ when it vanishes for all $x_1,\ldots,x_k\in M_nE^m$. **Minimal degree conjecture.** For all $n,m\geq 2$, the minimal degree of a standard identity that is a polynomial identity of $M_nE^m$ is

$$
2\left\lfloor\frac{m}{2}\right\rfloor+4n-4.
$$

The preceding lower bound shows that degree $2\left\lfloor\frac{m}{2}\right\rfloor+4n-5$ does not suffice, while the degree $4n-2$ upper bound settles the cases $m=2,3$; the conjecture predicts the exact degree for all $m,n\geq 2$.
record.source_name: Barbara Anna Balázs and Szabolcs Mészáros, “The Minimal Degree Standard Identity on M_nE^2 and M_nE^3”, arXiv:1901.07085 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.07085

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2019).

record.title: Ding–Li conjecture on Steiner systems from dual ternary codes
record.statement:
Let $m\ge 3$ be an odd integer, let $\alpha$ be a primitive element of $\operatorname{GF}(3^m)$, and let $\mathcal C_1$ and $\mathcal C_2$ be the ternary linear codes defined above. For $i\in\\{1,2\\}$, let $\mathcal C_i^{\perp}$ be the dual code, and let $\mathcal P(\mathcal C_i^{\perp})$ and $\mathcal B_4(\mathcal C_i^{\perp})$ denote its point set and the supports of its weight-$4$ codewords. **Ding–Li's Steiner-system conjecture.** Then

$$
(\mathcal P(\mathcal C_i^{\perp}),\mathcal B_4(\mathcal C_i^{\perp}))
$$

is a Steiner system $S(2,4,\frac{3^m-1}{2})$. The claim predicts Steiner systems obtained from the minimum-weight words of the dual codes; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Chunming Tang, Cunsheng Ding and Maosheng Xiong, “Steiner systems S(2, 4, 3^m-12) and 2-designs from ternary linear codes of length 3^m-12”, arXiv:1901.09228 (2019).

record.title: Erdős–Faudree–Győri minimum-book-number conjecture
record.statement:
Let $x\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $\frac12<x<1$, and let

$$
x=\prod_{i=1}^k\frac{r_i-1}{r_i}
$$

be its unique greedy representation, where $3\leq r_1$ and $(r_{i-1}-1)^2<r_i$ for $2\leq i\leq k$. Set

$$
b(x)=\prod_{i=1}^k\frac{r_i-2}{r_i}.
$$

For a graph, its book number is the maximum number of triangles containing one edge. **Erdős–Faudree–Győri conjecture.** Every graph on $n$ vertices with minimum degree $d\geq xn$ has book number at least $b(x)n$.

The conjecture asserts that the construction of Erdős, Faudree and Győri gives the correct minimum book number under a minimum-degree condition. The source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Victor Falgas–Ravry, Klas Markström and Yi Zhao, “Triangle-degrees in graphs and tetrahedron coverings in 3-graphs”, arXiv:1901.09560 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.09560

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2019).

record.title: Erdős–Faudree–Győri size-condition conjecture for book numbers
record.statement:
Let $x\in\mathbb{Q}\cap(\frac12,1)$, and let $b(x)$ be defined from the unique greedy representation

$$
x=\prod_{i=1}^k\frac{r_i-1}{r_i},\qquad 3\leq r_1,\quad (r_{i-1}-1)^2<r_i\ (2\leq i\leq k),
$$

by

$$
b(x)=\prod_{i=1}^k\frac{r_i-2}{r_i}.
$$

For a graph $G$, let $\mathrm{bk}(G)$ be its book number and define

$$
\beta(x):=\inf_n\{\mathrm{bk}(G)/n:v(G)=n,\ e(G)\geq x\binom n2\}.
$$

**Erdős–Faudree–Győri size-condition conjecture.**

$$
\beta(x)=b(x),
$$

i.e. every graph on $n$ vertices with at least $x\frac{n^2}{2}$ edges has book number at least $b(x)n$.

This conjecture proposes replacing the minimum-degree hypothesis in the preceding conjecture by an edge-density condition. The source reports supporting flag-algebra computations but no proof.
record.source_name: Victor Falgas–Ravry, Klas Markström and Yi Zhao, “Triangle-degrees in graphs and tetrahedron coverings in 3-graphs”, arXiv:1901.09560 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.09560

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2019).

record.title: Gupta's 1967 conjecture on multigraph edge-coloring
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a multigraph, write $\mu(G)=\mu$, and let $\Delta(G)$ denote its maximum degree. Assume that $\Delta(G)$ cannot be expressed as $2p\mu-q$ for integers satisfying $q\geq 0$ and $p>\lfloor(q+1)/2\rfloor$.

**Gupta's conjecture.** Then

$$
\chi'(G)\leq\Delta(G)+\mu(G)-1.
$$

The source states that this conjecture can be deduced from the Goldberg–Seymour conjecture, so it is solved in this paper's context.
record.source_name: Guantao Chen, Guangming Jing and Wenan Zang, “Proof of the Goldberg-Seymour Conjecture on Edge-Colorings of Multigraphs”, arXiv:1901.10316 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.10316

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2019). “The following two conjectures are due to Jakobsen and were proved by Andersen to be weaker than Conjecture .”

record.title: Thomassen's red-blue decomposition conjecture for 3-connected cubic graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a $3$-connected cubic graph on at least $8$ vertices. A red-blue vertex coloring partitions its vertices into red and blue classes; the blue subgraph is the subgraph induced by the blue vertices, and similarly for the red subgraph. **Thomassen's conjecture.** There is a red-blue vertex coloring of $G$ such that the blue subgraph has maximum degree at most $1$—that is, it consists of a matching and isolated vertices—while the red subgraph has minimum degree at least $1$ and contains no path with $4$ edges. The conjecture is a strengthening of a decomposition principle related to Wegner's square-coloring conjecture. The paper proves it for Generalized Petersen graphs, but the general statement is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: János Barát, “Decomposition of cubic graphs related to Wegner's conjecture”, arXiv:1901.11339 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.11339

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2019). “Therefore, it remains open whether the conjectured phenomenon in Conjecture generalizes to higher degrees.”

record.title: Balko et al.'s minimum Ramsey number conjecture for ordered paths
record.statement: Let $P_n$ be the path on $n$ vertices, and consider all orderings of its vertices. **Balko et al.'s conjecture.** Among all orderings of $P_n$, the alternating path has minimum Ramsey number. The conjecture concerns how the ordering of a graph affects its ordered Ramsey number. The source gives examples of orderings of $P_n$ with Ramsey numbers ranging from quadratic to linear, but does not state a resolution of this conjecture.

record.title: Rigidity conjecture for the Hausdorff dimension of symmetric limit sets
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma\subset \operatorname{SL}(n,\mathbb{R})$ be a projectively convex cocompact subgroup. Here $\delta_{1,n}$ is the critical exponent associated to the gap between the largest and smallest logarithmic singular values, $\xi^{sym}$ is the symmetric limit map, and $\partial_\infty\Gamma$ is the boundary of $\Gamma$. **Rigidity conjecture.** If

$$
2\delta_{1,n}=\operatorname{DimH}(\xi^{sym}(\partial_\infty\Gamma)),
$$

then $\Gamma$ is conjugate to a subgroup of $\operatorname{SO}(n-1,1)$. This conjecture extends rigidity results for groups preserving a non-degenerate quadratic form and for maximal surface-group representations; it predicts that equality in the Hausdorff-dimension inequality characterizes the hyperbolic subgroup case.
record.source_name: Olivier Glorieux, Daniel Monclair and Nicolas Tholozan, “Hausdorff dimension of limit sets for projective Anosov representations”, arXiv:1902.01844 (2023).

record.title: The proportionality conjecture for the sums $P_{n,t}$ and $A_n$
record.statement:
Let $g$ be the genus, let $n\geq 2$, and let $t\in\{0,\dots,n\}$. For integers $a_1,\dots,a_n\geq 0$ satisfying

$$
a_1+\cdots+a_n=2g-3+n,
$$

define $P_{n,t}$ by the preceding combinatorial sum and set

$$
A_n=(-1)^n(2g-4+n)!\sum_{\substack{o_1,\dots,o_n\in(2\mathbb{Z}+1)_{>0}\\o_1+\cdots+o_n=2g-4+n}}\prod_{j=1}^n\binom{2a_j}{o_j}.
$$

**Proportionality conjecture.** For every such $n$, $t$, and $(a_1,\dots,a_n)$, one has

$$
P_{n,t}=(-1)^t\left[\left(\binom{n-1}{t}-\binom{n-1}{t-1}\right)(2g-3+n+t)+2(t-1)\binom{n-1}{t-1}\right]A_n.
$$

This identity is a proposed combinatorial proportionality relating the quantities obtained by collecting terms according to the number of parity decreases to the basic odd-indexed sum $A_n$. The supplied source does not state whether the conjecture has been proved or refuted, so its resolution remains open.
record.source_name: Elba Garcia-Failde, Reinier Kramer, Danilo Lewański and Sergey Shadrin, “Half-Spin Tautological Relations and Faber's Proportionalities of Kappa Classes”, arXiv:1902.02742 (2019).
